attribution.note: Zitron directly asserts both proportional cost scaling and the exclusive causal explanation.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves linear scaling and the assertion that suppressed costs alone explain Q2 profitability.

contract.note: The proportional-cost reading and non-GAAP operating basis are reasonable. Adjusting for concessions respects the stated Q2 exception; holding services constant fairly tests the exclusive causal assertion.

evidence.note: Timely company disclosures show Q2 adjusted operating profit and a falling observed cost ratio. Without concession adjustments, these figures establish neither underlying proportional scaling nor the profitability counterfactual.

The contemporaneous report establishes reduced initial fees, but provides neither savings amounts nor comparable delivered capacity. It cannot establish that concessions were necessary for profitability.

reviews.rationale: The observed cost ratios decline, but the claim expressly treats discounted Q2 as an exception. No comparable adjusted series tests linear scaling, and no invoice-based counterfactual establishes whether ordinary fees would erase the disclosed $2.235 billion operating profit.

attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses the exclusive venture-capital explanation in his own prose.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves the ordinary assertion that both classes of commercial offerings depend universally on continuing venture-capital subsidies.

contract.note: Reading the listed prices as illustrative subscription tiers is ordinary in context. A sustainable, self-funded model provider fairly tests the categorical claim of necessary venture-capital support.

evidence.note: The dated report describes Midjourney as a profitable, self-funded model provider with no outside investors. It supplies the permitted reported counterexample, although its financial claims rely on company disclosures rather than audited accounts.

reviews.rationale: The packet documents a profitable commercial generative-AI provider operating without outside investment during the contract period. Under the fair reading of the prices as examples, this defeats universal venture-capital necessity. Missing audited accounts and exhaustive supplier-concession records limit certainty but do not establish such dependence.
